# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-18

**The Indonesia long-form is out and running hard: 17,061 views in its first 18 hours, already twice what “Ramayana’s Many Versions” has in ten days. The Ravana long-form is due tomorrow with no long-form draft on disk. The last film Short failed its day-three check.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish the Ravana fact-check long-form: who first argued that Ravana was the wronged side.** (long, due 2026-11-19, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Due tomorrow, four days open, and the only thing on disk is the Shorts script on E. V. Ramasamy. The case got stronger overnight: the Indonesia long-form, a Ramayana video whose title states a claim, reached 17,061 views in 18 hours, and the three Ravana Shorts still have no long-form behind them.  
   First step: Say yes or no today. Yes: write the first minute tonight, the 1882 sentence on screen and its author named after it. No: mark it Drop on the Brief tab so the slot goes to something that will ship.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Two days left and nothing is scripted. The Karnataka row over his legacy is the peg, and the owner's note of 15 November sets the story: the prize money and palace treasure taken on 4 May 1799, then the British writing of Tipu as a tyrant. His birth date is disputed, so the Short rests on the news, not on the birthday.  
   First step: Script and record today. Sentence one is one sum or one object from the prize records that shows who got rich, checked against the original. Publish Friday 20 November an hour or two before 18:00 IST.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: It is the top-ranked dated moment of the next three weeks and it sits with Aurangzeb, the subject of the channel's two largest videos. Videos that size brought 66.4% of lifetime subscribers, and this month none has come: 0 subscribers against 1,185 planned from them.  
   First step: Have the script on disk by 19 November: sentence one is the order, the place and the date, told as an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Record by 21 November, publish the evening of 23 November.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
17,700 subscribers against a target of 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 19,205, which needs 57.5 net a day; the 7-day rate is 83.4 and the 28-day rate 39.3. Projection basis: 28-day rate; the 7-day rate is a spike. On that basis the month ends at 18,171, 1,034 short, and the channel is 766 behind the ramp today. The 7-day rate rests on the film week, so do not read it as the new normal, and uploads account for 43.2% of net subscribers over 28 days, under half, so the rate also rests on growth outside the videos that can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts: 0 subscribers against 1,185 targeted this month. 0.85 of a breakout at the median 1,393 subs. The demonstrated route is a newsjack of a mass release (Chhava gave three of four) or an evergreen controversy with a searchable name; check the calendar and news releases for the next peg. Analytics runs to 2026-11-15, two days before the Indonesia launch: on that count long-form did 57,484 views in 7 days, down 18.5% on the week before, and Shorts did 139,266 against 53,374. The Indonesia video's subscribers are not in the data yet; they arrive with Analytics in two to three days. Last week every Short that beat the usual was about Ravana and both that fell short were about the film or the Constitution, which is why the Ravana long-form stays first.

What's working
- “How Indonesia Became Muslim: The Ramayana Was REWRITTEN” has 17,061 views at 938.2 an hour, with a like rate of 1.9% against 1.0% for “Ramayana’s Many Versions” and 0.9% for the Asia long-form. It is the first of the three Ramayana long-forms whose title states a claim and whose opening names who did what. Day one is mostly subscribers; the reading that counts is day three, 20 November.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11.8 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape of the Ravana long-form: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
- “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” keeps earning from search: 9,856 views and still several hundred a day on the last day counted, twelve days after release. A Short that answers a searched name keeps working.

What's wrong
- The Ravana long-form has been first on this list for four days and has not started. Probable cause: the Indonesia launch took the week, which was the right call on today's numbers. Test: none needed. It needs a yes or a no today; left alone it lapses on 22 November.
- Film reach is still not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8.4, and only 41.4% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of the fall is how views are now counted. Probable cause: the film videos answer a scene or tour a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Indonesia long-form names one. On day three compare its net subscribers per 1,000 with the Asia long-form's.
- The last film Short failed its day-three check: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” has 1,533 views, under the usual for a Short. Probable cause: its title is about the film's rule, not a person or a claim, and the Short before it on Rama in the Constitution fell short the same way. As yesterday's brief set out, the film window is closed for Shorts about the film itself. The Indonesia launch shows it is not closed for a Ramayana claim.
- “Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,426 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000, ten days after release, with an average view of 27.8%. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: at day three, compare the Indonesia long-form's first drop after the opening with the 14 points this one lost at 0:35.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-15. Long-form is still a Home-feed channel: 148,574 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 4,072 from search. Shorts drew 27.7% of their views from search over 28 days; the finding that search carries the Shorts has fallen out of range, because the film Shorts rode the Shorts feed.
- The film is now news in Indonesia itself. Today's headlines report fans dressed as Hindu gods at screenings there, and the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is still at 2.85x its 30-day median. That is the same audience the Indonesia long-form speaks to, on the day after it went up.
- Search for the long-forms is small: 4,072 views over 28 days. The Indonesia title was chosen partly for search, so do not expect search to show in its first week; if it helps, it shows over months.
- WhatsApp referred 12,508 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 442; the base is views from outside YouTube, a small part of all views. If the Indonesia long-form has not gone out on WhatsApp yet, today is still inside its first two days.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form has drawn many comments since launch, but only a handful are in the data yet, so there is no reading of them today. Under the Ravana Shorts the argument is still about motive, and some viewers read the film's Ravana as a political hero, which is what the Ravana long-form answers.
- **The film swapped lust for revenge** (mixed): "the core reason for why he abducted Sita Ji is for lust and arrogance, now in Namit Malhotra's Ramayana they properly showed the arrogance part but replaced lust with revenge which leads to the controversy"
- **Viewers see a political Ravana in the film** (negative): "New movie is woke Ramayana, comrade Ravana freeing oppressed Rakshahas from Deva, they projected Lanka as communist utopia."
- **Requests for Hindi** (neutral): "Vai, aap hindi mee bhi video banao na. English mee problem hota hya"

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola's fleet to Srivijaya, as the answer to “never sent a single soldier”
- Reliable historians to read on the older kingdoms, asked under the Indonesia long-form
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one

## Competitors
Thirteen days after release the watchlist is still on the film, mostly as reaction and verdict. Nobody on the list has traced where the sympathetic Ravana came from, and nobody has a second video on the Ramayana outside India.
- **Upword**: "An eight-year-old watched Ramayana and liked Ravan more than Shri Ram!"
  Why it worked: 23,312 views at 3.9x the channel's median, on the exact feeling the Ravana long-form answers: a viewer who came out of the film on Ravana's side.
  Steal: Put that viewer in the Ravana long-form's title or thumbnail: the person who liked Ravana, and the 1882 book behind the feeling.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 160,127 views at 31.6x, the list's top outlier. It opens by saying the claim it attacks in full and answers from there.
  Steal: Open the Ravana long-form on the sympathetic claim in its own words, said straight, and turn on it in the next sentence.

Gaps
- Where the sympathetic Ravana came from, with names and dates: three own Shorts, an Upword outlier and the month's search terms point at it, and nobody on the list has the long-form.
- Direct Action Day in long-form: the channel's own search data shows demand for “direct action day” arriving only at its three Shorts on it.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: The Ramayana film in Indonesia: fans dressed as Hindu gods at screenings  
  Signal: In today's headlines from India Today and Gulf News, one day after the Indonesia long-form went up at 938.2 views an hour. (News, own launch data)  
  Make: No decision slot is free, so this is the one extra worth an hour: cut one Short from the long-form's own opening, Ravana asking for his powers and who grants them, and set the long-form as its Related video. Publish by 19 November while the screenings are in the news. Do not write a new script for it.
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: two days, no Short scripted  
  Signal: The Karnataka row over his legacy is the peg; the radar's step for this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”. (Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November)  
  Make: Decision 2, in dates: script and record today, publish Friday 20 November an hour or two before 18:00 IST, judge on 23 November. Keep “Tipu Sultan” at the front of the title.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: The top-ranked dated moment, six days out; the radar's step is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Decision 3, in dates: script by 19 November, record by 21, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26.
- **watch, short, 2/5**: Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, in cinemas 4 December  
  Signal: A war film on the radar with no confirmed subject. Its first step opens on 20 November. (Moments radar)  
  Make: Before 20 November, check what real event, if any, the film is about. A real war with an Indian side and a named enemy makes it the next mass-release peg; fiction means skip it.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: Birsa Munda and Nehru on Wikipedia  
  Signal: Birsa Munda's Hindi page is at 31.71x its median and Nehru's at 23.9x. Both follow their dates of 15 and 14 November, which have passed. (Wikipedia pageviews, calendar)  
  Make: Skip. The dates are gone and both spikes are the anniversary itself, not a new question. A Birsa Munda film is announced for 2027; that is the time for him.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [4/5, long] **Who Made Ravana the Wronged Hero? It Began With a British Book in 1882**  
  Decolonization reframe; Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named author convicted from his own page; Contested history  
  source: Decision 1
- [3/5, short] **Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It**  
  Empire and extraction: the prize money and the palace treasure; Contested history: the Karnataka row; Villain plus hypocrisy: the men who took the treasure wrote the verdict on him  
  source: Decision 2. Owner pick of 15 November.
- [3/5, short] **Guru Tegh Bahadur: Aurangzeb's Order, Chandni Chowk, 1675**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named emperor and a dated order; Contested history  
  source: Decision 3
- [3/5, long] **Why Bali Is Still Hindu: The Priests Who Left Java**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Hidden history: the other half of the Indonesia story; Villain: the sultanates named in the Indonesia long-form  
  source: New today, from the Indonesia launch. Not to be started before its day-three reading on 20 November; if the launch holds, this is the follow-on its viewers are most likely to want.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,376 followers, up 250 in 7 days, 35.7 a day. The latest reel, “Every Ramayan kept one rule. The New Namit Malhotra film broke it.”, has reached 11,579 with a skip rate of 40.4% against a reel median of 54.1%. Carousels remain the growth format at 3.77x the median reach of reels. Correction: yesterday's brief attached the evidence lines for card count and for the revision lane to each other's action; they are the right way round below.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 38 followers (91 posts); outside the band, 12 (14 posts). Pooled rate 3.01 vs 1.52 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 376 followers a month at stake.
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  52 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.85 vs 2.12 per 1k. 376 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  18 of 103 rated posts are shared above the median (26.1/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 13.1k reach for a median 13 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 895 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 82.4k reach between them and 117 followers, 1.3 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 160.1. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 92 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Add one line under the pinned comment on “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” pointing to the Indonesia long-form, and put the Indonesia long-form on its end screen.  
  The Asia long-form is the channel's largest long-form audience, at 154,574 views, and its viewers are the ones most likely to want the sequel.
- **this_week**: Read the title and thumbnail test on the Indonesia long-form on 20 November, not before. If one pair is still clearly last, stop the test and rerun it with the other two.  
  On day one the three pairs were close and the Indonesia-led title was last. Day one is mostly subscribers; the Home-feed audience decides it.
- **this_week**: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.  
  They stand at 78 and 255 views two weeks on. Still open.
- **later**: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.  
  Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.
